package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions contain a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2019-7238) that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server via a crafted HTTP request. While the package itself is not intentionally malicious, the vulnerability enables malicious exploitation, making unpatched versions dangerous in production environments.

execution_context.file_location: Core REST API endpoint (undisclosed internal Java class)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request to a vulnerable REST API endpoint, which is improperly validated and allows arbitrary code execution on the server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Processes attacker-controlled input in a REST API endpoint, leading to arbitrary code execution on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The REST API endpoint fails to properly validate or sanitize user input, allowing attackers to inject and execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal REST API endpoints should strictly validate and sanitize all input, never allowing user-supplied data to be executed as code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate REST APIs may process user input, but should never execute it as code.
key_indicators: Remote code execution via HTTP request
Ability to execute arbitrary commands on the server

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers a vulnerable instance of Nexus Repository Manager 3 running a version prior to 3.15.
Attacker crafts and sends a malicious HTTP request to the vulnerable REST API endpoint.
The server processes the malicious request, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the Nexus Repository process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential full system compromise, data exfiltration, or further lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected process execution by the Nexus Repository Manager process
Unusual outbound network connections initiated by the repository server
Abnormal HTTP requests to REST API endpoints with suspicious payloads
file_indicators: Unexpected files or scripts appearing in the server filesystem
Modifications to configuration or binary files outside of normal upgrade cycles
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections from the repository server to external IPs
Inbound HTTP requests to REST API endpoints with atypical or malformed payloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for abnormal process execution and network activity originating from the Nexus Repository Manager process. Inspect HTTP access logs for suspicious or malformed requests to REST API endpoints. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unexpected changes to the server filesystem. Ensure all instances are upgraded to version 3.15 or later to eliminate the vulnerability.
